Q: What is Category 5 (Cat 5) cable commonly used for today?
Option1: High speed 10 Gigabit Ethernet for 100 meters
Option2: Older Fast Ethernet up to 100 Mb/s; largely replaced by newer categories

Q: What improvement does Category 5e (Cat 5e) add over Cat 5?
Option1: Supports up to 1 Gb/s Ethernet on typical runs with reduced crosstalk
Option2: Adds fiber strands to the cable

Q: Which statement about Category 6 (Cat 6) is accurate?
Option1: Only supports 100 Mb/s
Option2: Supports 1 Gb/s to 100 m and 10 Gb/s for shorter distances

Q: What distinguishes Category 6a (Cat 6a) from Cat 6?
Option1: Designed to support 10 Gb/s to 100 meters
Option2: Removes twisted pairs

Q: What is coaxial cable most often used for in networks?
Option1: Short fiber jumpers
Option2: Cable internet and television distribution using F type connectors

Q: What is shielded twisted pair (STP)?
Option1: Twisted pair with additional shielding around pairs or bundle to reduce interference
Option2: A fiber optic cable type

Q: What does 'direct burial' mean on copper cabling?
Option1: Cable designed for plenum spaces
Option2: Cable rated to be buried in the ground without conduit and with moisture protection

Q: What is unshielded twisted pair (UTP)?
Option1: Coaxial with no braid
Option2: Standard Ethernet cable with twisted pairs and no additional shielding

Q: What is 'plenum rated' cable?
Option1: Cable designed for outdoor conduit only
Option2: Jacket that produces low smoke and toxic fumes when heated, required in air handling spaces

Q: What is the primary advantage of optical fiber in networking?
Option1: Works only for short distances
Option2: Immunity to electromagnetic interference and very long distance, high bandwidth transmission using light

Q: What are T568A and T568B?
Option1: Fiber polishing methods
Option2: Ethernet copper pinout standards defining pair order in 8P8C connectors

Q: For a straight through patch cable, which termination rule is correct?
Option1: Use T568A on one end and T568B on the other
Option2: Use the same standard on both ends, either T568A or T568B

Q: Which video interface carries digital video and audio on a single cable and is common on TVs?
Option1: Video Graphics Array (VGA)
Option2: High Definition Multimedia Interface (HDMI)

Q: Which interface supports packet based video, daisy chaining, and high resolutions on computers?
Option1: DisplayPort
Option2: RJ45

Q: Which legacy video interface is analog only and uses a 15 pin D sub connector?
Option1: Video Graphics Array (VGA)
Option2: High Definition Multimedia Interface

Q: What is Digital Visual Interface (DVI)?
Option1: Analog only signaling
Option2: A digital or analog video interface with variants such as DVI D and DVI I

Q: Which storage cable is most common for modern internal drives?
Option1: Integrated Drive Electronics (IDE or PATA) ribbon
Option2: Serial Advanced Technology Attachment (SATA) 7 pin data cable
Option3: Small Computer System Interface (SCSI) parallel cable

Q: What is External SATA (eSATA) used for?
Option1: Internal motherboard to drive links only
Option2: Connecting external SATA storage with a shielded connector

Q: What is Small Computer System Interface (SCSI) in this context?
Option1: A modern consumer video port
Option2: A legacy parallel or serial storage interface historically used in servers and workstations

Q: What is Integrated Drive Electronics (IDE or PATA)?
Option1: Parallel ribbon cable interface for older drives with 40 pin connectors
Option2: New serial interface for 10 Gb/s drives

Q: What is Universal Serial Bus (USB) 2.0 best described as?
Option1: Up to 480 Mb/s peripheral interface
Option2: 10 Gb/s optical link

Q: What key change did USB 3.x introduce over USB 2.0?
Option1: Lower speed
Option2: Higher throughput in gigabits per second and additional pins on many connectors

Q: What is 'serial' in the peripheral list referring to?
Option1: Parallel printer port
Option2: RS 232 communications commonly using a DB9 connector for legacy devices

Q: What is Thunderbolt used for?
Option1: Low speed peripherals only
Option2: High speed external interface carrying PCI Express and DisplayPort over Mini DisplayPort or USB C connectors

Q: What is an adapter in this section?
Option1: A device that converts one physical interface to another or allows connection between different connector types
Option2: A cable tester

Q: Which connector is 'RJ11' typically used with?
Option1: Ethernet
Option2: Telephone lines for analog or digital voice

Q: Which connector is 'RJ45' commonly associated with?
Option1: Ethernet 8 position 8 contact modular connector
Option2: Telephone handsets

Q: What is an F type connector used for?
Option1: USB cables
Option2: Coaxial connections such as cable TV and cable modems

Q: What is the Straight Tip (ST) connector?
Option1: A fiber optic bayonet style connector
Option2: A coax crimp connector

Q: What is the Subscriber Connector (SC)?
Option1: A copper telephone plug
Option2: A square push pull fiber optic connector

Q: What is the Lucent Connector (LC)?
Option1: A small form factor fiber optic connector often used in duplex pairs
Option2: A coax TV connector

Q: What is a punchdown block in this context?
Option1: A video adapter
Option2: A termination block (for example 66 or 110) where twisted pair conductors are seated with a punchdown tool

Q: What is a Molex connector used for?
Option1: Legacy 4 pin power connector for internal drives and fans
Option2: Modern SATA data connection

Q: What is Apple Lightning?
Option1: A fiber optic plug
Option2: A proprietary reversible power and data connector used on some Apple mobile devices

Q: What is DB9?
Option1: Nine pin D sub connector commonly used for RS 232 serial connections
Option2: A fiber coupler

Q: What is microUSB used for in this context?
Option1: Legacy small USB connector for many phones and peripherals, supports data and power
Option2: Fiber optic jumper

Q: What is miniUSB?
Option1: Smaller legacy USB connector used on older cameras/peripherals before microUSB
Option2: Modern reversible USB connector

Q: What is USB-C?
Option1: Reversible USB connector that can carry data, power, and alternate modes (for example, DisplayPort/Thunderbolt)
Option2: A fiber SC connector

Q: Which statement compares UTP and STP correctly?
Option1: UTP has no additional shielding; STP adds foil/braid shielding to reduce interference
Option2: Both are fiber types
Option3: UTP is only for telephone lines

Q: Which situation calls for plenum-rated cable rather than riser or general-purpose?
Option1: In return-air spaces where low-smoke, low-toxicity jackets are required by code
Option2: Outdoor aerial spans only

Q: Which situation calls for direct-burial cable?
Option1: Cabling laid underground without conduit with moisture protection
Option2: Cabling above drop ceilings
Option3: Short patch leads between a switch and a server

Q: When would a passive display adapter (for example, DisplayPort-to-HDMI) work without external power?
Option1: When the source port supports the required alternate mode and signal type natively
Option2: Only when converting analog VGA to digital
